title: Mirabel and the Hollow
premise: Wren Okafor, a beast-speaker concealing his forbidden gift while keeping the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, is drawn into danger when a mute child arrives at the guildhouse speaking a language older than any kingdom. The child's words are a living key to the Hollow — an ancient power beneath the free cities that the usurper Veyran intends to wake and weaponize. Hunted by Veyran's inquisitors and betrayed by the guildmaster who sold them out, Wren must choose between exposing his gift to save the child or staying silent while the war reignites. In the end, Wren speaks with the Hollow itself, binding its power to justice rather than conquest at the cost of his own voice, leaving the free cities saved but forever changed.
about_author: Emrys Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval trade ledgers before turning to fantasy. They write stories about ordinary keepers of records caught in extraordinary histories.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We meet Wren balancing the Guild of Impossible Things' ledgers by day and secretly trading words with rats and gulls by night, hiding a gift that once got his village burned. When a debt collector threatens to expose him, he pays with silence. Emotional beat: weary vigilance, the cost of hiding.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A mud-caked child appears at the guildhouse door during a storm, speaking no known tongue — yet Wren's gift hears meaning in it: a name for something buried. He hides the child from the gatekeeper. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness awakening old fear.

chapters.title: What the Rats Remember
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Questioning the city's animals, Wren learns the child walked out of the Ashfen, where nothing lives, followed by things that should not move. The child draws spirals matching marks in the guild's oldest ledger. Emotional beat: dawning dread that his secret and the child's are entangled.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Smile
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane's POV. Corvane notices the child and quietly sends word to the capital, weighing the guild's survival against one stray life. His chapter reveals the guild has traded with Veyran's regime before. Emotional beat: cold pragmatism dressed as care.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Grey
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Sera Grey's POV. Grey arrives hunting beast-speakers, carrying a warrant and a personal grudge against the gift that killed her brother. She interrogates the guildhouse staff; Wren lies well but not perfectly. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension, a worthy adversary introduced.

chapters.title: The Word Beneath Words
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Through fragments of the child's ancient language, Wren pieces together the story of the Hollow: a power sealed beneath the free cities after the first war, kept dormant by speakers like him. The child is its last warden's heir. Emotional beat: awe curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Fen
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered through Wren's translation). A flashback-chapter: the child's village destroyed by Veyran's excavators digging for the Hollow, the wardens slaughtered, the child sent away with the language in their blood. Emotional beat: grief as fuel.

chapters.title: Sold at Midnight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvane sells the child's location to Grey's agents. Warned by a dying pigeon, Wren flees with the child through the guild's smugglers' tunnels, abandoning the only life he built. Emotional beat: betrayal, and liberation in losing everything.

chapters.title: The Free Cities at Dusk
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided: refugees choke the roads, Veyran's armies mass beyond the passes, and city councils argue over surrender. Wren sees the stakes are larger than one child. Emotional beat: the world tilting toward war.

chapters.title: Thieves Who Owe Him
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren calls in favors from the underworld — a fence, a disgraced knight, a rat-queen of the sewers — forming a ragged circle of protectors. Each owes him a debt from his ledger days. Emotional beat: found family forged from transaction.

chapters.title: Grey's Doubt
chapters.summary: Sera Grey's POV. Grey finds evidence that Veyran's excavations, not beast-speakers, caused the Ashfen massacre. Her certainty cracks; she conceals a report for the first time in her career. Emotional beat: a lawwoman discovering the law serves the wrong master.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Ear
chapters.summary: Veyran's POV. The usurper learns the warden-child lives and orders the Hollow opened before winter, believing its power will make resistance impossible. His chapter shows a man who mistakes ownership for control. Emotional beat: ambition hollowing into madness.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of Roots
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hiding in an abandoned grove-shrine, Wren teaches the child common speech while the child teaches him the Hollow's true nature: not a weapon but a wounded thing that remembers every broken promise. Emotional beat: quiet bond deepening before the storm.

chapters.title: The Circle Breaks
chapters.summary: Grey's POV. Grey tracks the fugitives but instead finds Corvane's second betrayal — a bounty on Wren dead, not alive. She lets the trail go cold and burns her warrant. Emotional beat: defection, chosen alone.

chapters.title: March of the Iron Bells
chapters.summary: Braided POVs. Veyran's vanguard reaches the outer free city; bells ring retreat; the council surrenders one city to buy time. Wren realizes negotiation is dead — only the Hollow can stop the army, and waking it may destroy everything. Emotional beat: despair sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Guided by the child and every creature of the dark, Wren descends into the Hollow's seal beneath the surrendered city, past bones of the first war's dead. Grey intercepts them — and stands aside, then joins. Emotional beat: terror met with courage.

chapters.title: The Hollow Speaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Hollow tests Wren, offering him power to remake the world and punish his enemies. He refuses domination and offers instead witness: to speak its grief aloud so it can be mourned, not weaponized. Emotional beat: temptation overcome by humility.

chapters.title: Veyran at the Gate
chapters.summary: Veyran's POV and Wren's intercut. The usurper breaches the seal chamber with excavator-machines and demands the Hollow kneel. It answers with the accumulated weight of every promise he broke. Emotional beat: tyrant unmade by his own record.

chapters.title: The Price of a Voice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. To reseal the Hollow safely, someone must give it their voice as anchor. Wren speaks the binding — sacrificing his gift, perhaps permanently — as the army breaks and the child completes the wardens' song. Emotional beat: sacrifice without bitterness.

chapters.title: After the Bells Fall Silent
chapters.summary: Grey's POV. The free cities reckon with what nearly happened; Grey testifies against Corvane and the collaborators, building justice outside the collapsed courts. Veyran's remnant scatters. Emotional beat: exhausted, hard-won accountability.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns to a half-burned guildhouse, keeps the ledgers still, and discovers small sounds remain to him — enough to hear the child laugh, if not the sparrows. Some debts were worth paying everything for. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace.

chapters.title: The First Word of Spring
chapters.summary: Child's POV, now fluent in two tongues. The child, adopted by the rebuilt community, plants a tree over the sealed Hollow and speaks its first word of the new season. Far below, something sleeps content. Emotional beat: renewal, and a door left gently ajar.
